channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Insurance – Long-term disability benefits
item.description: Where a plaintiff has brought suit over a denial of long-term disability benefits, a remand for further review is appropriate because the defendant insurer gave undue weight to surveillance videos and improperly rejected much of the evidence that the plaintiff submitted.

item.title: Civil practice – Deliberative process privilege
item.description: Where intervenors have requested access to trial exhibits and provisionally sealed pleadings, that request should be granted because the deliberative process privilege does not apply.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Abstention
item.description: Where a complaint was filed following the entry of a Massachusetts Juvenile Court order granting custody of a child to her father in Guatemala, the complaint must be dismissed for lack of jurisdiction under the abstention doctrine.

item.title: Freedom of information – FACA – Emails
item.description: Where plaintiffs have moved to compel disclosure of records under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, all 19 disputed emails authored by Climate Working Group members must be disclosed in their entirety, with the names of the reviewers of the draft report disclosed, but the reviewers’ personal information may properly be withheld.

item.title: Immigration – Habeas corpus
item.description: Where a petitioner from Vietnam has alleged that he is being unlawfully detained, his habeas corpus petition should be granted because the respondents have not established a reasonable likelihood of the petitioner’s removal in the foreseeable future pursuant to 8 C.F.R. §241.13(i)(2).

item.title: Immigration – Parole
item.description: Where a class action has been brought challenging steps taken by the Department of Homeland Security to terminate humanitarian parole programs, the plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction should be allowed because the plaintiffs have demonstrated a strong likelihood that they will prevail on their claim that the termination of existing awards of parole was arbitrary and capricious.

item.title: Negligence – Slip and fall
item.description: Where a plaintiff who fell while shopping inside one of the defendant’s stores has brought a negligence suit alleging that the defendant failed to maintain its premises in a reasonably safe condition, the defendant’s motion for summary judgment should be allowed because the plaintiff has not put forward evidence that any dangerous condition existed or that the defendant was on notice of one.

item.title: Consumer protection – FDCPA – TILA
item.description: Where two defendants have moved to dismiss a Fair Debt Collection Practice Act complaint, that motion should be allowed because the plaintiff has not identified a creditor or other entity that violated §1637(b) of the Truth in Lending Act.

item.title: Civil practice – Asset freeze – Preliminary injunction
item.description: Where a plaintiff has moved for a preliminary injunction seeking to prevent the defendants from transferring or encumbering their assets, the motion should be denied because the plaintiff has not shown the “strong indication” that the defendants may dissipate or conceal assets that is necessary to establish irreparable harm.

item.title: Taxation – Corporate excise – Deduction
item.description: Where a corporation sought to deduct an expense for subcontractors purportedly paid in cash, the commissioner of revenue’s denial of that request should be upheld because the corporation failed to substantiate the cash wages it claimed to have paid to its workers in 2015.
